name: Ken and Mary Tree

location.address: Patchwork Road area, Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido

access: Free. Stands beside a farm field on the open hillside; viewable from the roadside, no entry restriction.
transport: Reached by car or rental bicycle along Biei's 'Patchwork Road', roughly 20 to 30 minutes from central Biei.
verify_notes: Standalone destination tree, qualifying on historical/cultural significance rather than extreme age: a single tall poplar planted originally as a boundary marker between two farm fields, which became famous nationwide after appearing in a 1972 Nissan Skyline television commercial starring characters nicknamed 'Ken' and 'Mary'. It gave the tree its name and turned it into one of the most photographed single trees in Hokkaido, an emblem of the Biei hill-farm landscape (Patchwork Road). Confirmed still standing and healthy as of recent (2024-era) local tourism sources, in contrast to two other once-famous Biei roadside trees, the 'Tree of Philosophy' (felled) and the Mild Seven Hills' poplar avenue (thinned), which the tree survived while they did not. Height approximately 30m, age over a century (roughly 100+ years), species a poplar (exact cultivar not established in sources checked, hence Populus sp. and no girth recorded). Flagged for the unestablished exact species/cultivar and for the lack of a precise planting date.
